correctness.rationale: For the cone over the rectangle, crepant rays are at height one; every height-one lattice point must occur in a smooth subdivision, since in a unimodular cone its nonnegative integral coordinates sum to one. Thus the labeled smooth crepant fans are exactly the unimodular triangulations using all 12 points, and relative projectivity corresponds to a coherent lifting. A coherent coarsening with one quadrilateral admits the two small projective refinements: no ray changes, and the single affine dependence gives one wall and a crepant flop. Conversely any adjacency of the stipulated kind must exchange the diagonals of one such quadrilateral. The independent exact replay, /workspace/branches/b9fa7f38-e9cf-4697-b538-a765f43ce391/independent_replay.py and full_replay.log, reads the frozen JSON strictly as data. It reconstructed 852 distinct triangulations, each with 12 normalized-area-one triangles, exhausting the independently known count f(2,3). It rebuilt every legal exchange, found 2626, and checked each integral height vector: all 852 triangulations have strict lower triangles, while all 2626 walls have ten strict common triangles and exactly their four quadrilateral vertices coplanar on the remaining lower face. Full-graph BFS from every vertex gave radius 10, diameter 20 and the unique pair 0x8c3c04117, 0x71885e0820. The log confirms the stated histogram, including 180 vertices of degree 6. No frozen script was executed. This verifies the relative toric graph only, not arbitrary nontoric resolutions.

value.rationale: The first rectangle beyond the 2 by 2 width-two square is a natural tractable relative toric phase graph, with a known census but no metric profile in the earlier inspected results. The exact diameter gives the optimal bound on elementary flops over the original affine base, the unique pair identifies the sole extremal obstruction, and the lifts verify that the counted paths do not use abstract but nonprojective flips. These precise data are usable in comparisons and benchmark calculations independently of a broader theorem.
